title: Adapter Program: Quick-win Playbook (prototype)
body:
Objective:
- Give sellers and SEs a compact, repeatable playbook to run 2-week adapter/pilot engagements with platform teams and ISVs.
- Focus: convert technical integrators who need low-friction routing + cost predictability into committed pilots for Dedicated or Private.

Audience (persona slices):
- Integration Architect (primary): cares about latency SLOs, predictable unit economics, routing policies.
- Platform Engineer (secondary): needs automation hooks, rollout safety, observability.
- Product Manager (decision influencer): ROI on user-facing features, error modes.

One-line value:
- Show them a 2-week integration that proves latency under load, fallback resilience, and monthly cost estimates — with a low-risk canary and rollback path.

Slide 1: Why run an adapter pilot (seller opener)
- Quick win: shipping an embed or routed endpoint in 2 weeks
- Risk reduction: canary + automatic fallback to cheaper model variants
- Outcome: measurable latency & cost delta vs in-house GPU ops
- Hook: show a single graph (99th P50 latencies + cost per 1k tokens)

Slide 2: Target signals to qualify (fast checklist)
- Existing API-based inference or microservice architecture
- ~80–500 RPS expected during PoC window OR bursty workflows that need autoscale
- Compliance note: customer willing to run canary on Redwood Dedicated or Private

Slide 3: Two-week pilot timeline (day-by-day summary)
- Day 0: kickoff, alignment on SLOs, access & test data exchange
- Day 1–3: quick integration, model selection + baseline perf run (customer env)
- Day 4–7: enable routing, prefix/KV cache config, simple batching suggestions
- Day 8–10: simulated load & cost projection run (outline methodology)
- Day 11–13: canary to production path, docs handoff, runbook prep
- Day 14: results review, contract/next-step proposal

Slide 4: Minimal technical checklist for SEs (scripted stepper)
- Ask for: sample traffic (anonymized), typical prompt lengths, worst-case context length
- Confirm: network egress path, auth (API keys), and logging retention needs
- Baseline: run baseline 10k tokens through their current infra (or partner)
- Redwood steps: spin model variant, set batching window, enable prefix cache, set routing priority rules
- Observability: wire token-level tracing + latency breakdown to Console

Slide 5: Demo script (6 minutes)
- Minute 0–1: quick problem statement + live dashboard showing request queue
- Minute 1–3: run a sample prompt and show streaming + KV cache hit behavior
- Minute 3–5: flip routing policy to cheaper variant and demonstrate fallback in 30s
- Minute 5–6: show SLO dashboard and cost projection widget

Slide 6: Seller talking points (short bullets)
- No infra lift: Redwood handles model serving and routing, you keep control of data flows
- Predictable economics: we give a per-route cost projection after a 10k token run
- Graceful degradation: automatic fallbacks keep user-facing features alive during capacity pressure
- Security: option to run in VPC or Private with KMS integration

Slide 7: Risk & objections (prep for rebuttals)
- “We can’t trust a managed provider with latency-sensitive paths” -> Demo single-digit retry + fallback, offer Dedicated pilot with SLA window.
- “Cost looks unpredictable” -> Show historical cost projection approach and how batching reduces unit cost.
- “We have a blackbox model” -> Suggest model-variant mapping and staged rollout (A/B by tenant).

Slide 8: Success metrics we propose
- Performance: meet agreed 99th percentile latency SLO during baseline and under 2× expected load
- Reliability: <1% requests routed to fallback in steady-state after tuning
- Cost: projected per-1k-token unit cost vs current baseline with >=15% improvement target depending on workload
- Business: conversion to reserved capacity / commitment or platform contract within 60 days

Slide 9: Artifacts we deliver at handoff
- Handoff doc with model & quant settings, batching & cache configs
- Runbook: canary checklist, rollback commands, observability queries (Console links)
- Cost projection spreadsheet + assumptions

Slide 10: Fast appendix for SEs
- SDK snippets (curl + python) for embedding calls
- Minimal IAM checklist for Private/Dedicated onboarding
- Quick table: recommended model families by workload (short prompts vs long context)

Notes to self / open questions (internal)
- Experiment: add a short-risk-simulate harness for platform teams to emulate degraded GPU capacity and validate fallback latencies (INFER-3421 in Jira).
- Need PR to seller-assets repo: add the 6-min demo script + dashboard screenshots (see linked PR).
- Align with Solutions Eng on any required legal language for pilots running on Dedicated.

Action items (next 7 days)
- [Aisha] finalize demo notebook & dashboard filters (due 2025-09-26)
- [Jon] draft pilot statement of work (SOW) template (due 2025-09-30)
- [Marta] create follow-up email template and ROI one-pager (due 2025-10-02)

Slack channels / threads to reference:
- #se-adapter-program (active pilot coordination)
- #prod-oncall for any canary issues

Quick links (for seller pack)
- Quickstart: https://docs.redwood.ai/quickstart/adapters
- Cost projection tool: https://console.redwood.ai/cost-proj

End note: this is intentionally compact — keep the playbook to 1 slide per topic when presenting to buyers, keep demo tight, and aim for a decision or calendared next-step at the end of the 2-week window.
